key_insight: The paper proves a spatial symmetry invariance theorem stating that exact solutions of deterministic 3D Navier–Stokes equations with periodic boundaries preserve the spatial symmetries of their initial flow.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry preservation offers a benchmark for detecting numerical contamination in CFD simulations of turbulent flows.
method: Establish a spatial symmetry invariance theorem for periodic 3D Navier–Stokes flow.
Test traditional DNS against exact symmetry preservation.
Examine numerical-noise effects on turbulent trajectories and statistics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that traditional DNS quickly violates symmetry invariance and that even statistical results can depend sensitively on initial conditions, but provides no quantitative error or convergence data.
watch_item: Apply the benchmark only under the theorem’s assumptions; symmetry loss alone does not quantify errors in all turbulence statistics.
paper_title: Spatial symmetry invariance of three-dimensional Navier-Stokes turbulence
